subject: ACME: evidence request — cookies & marketing telemetry for DPA
body:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-marketing.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — cookies & marketing telemetry for DPA

Hi Ben / Marissa,

We're working through a routine DPA / vendor evidence request ahead of our Q2 audit and we need a short package from Redwood covering how marketing-related telemetry and client-side cookies are handled. Our legal and privacy team have a few specific asks so we can close the vendor risk assessment:

- A current list of subprocessors involved in collecting or processing marketing telemetry (SDKs, analytics backends, third-party services).
- Data transfer guidance: which customer telemetry data (if any) is transferred outside the EU, and which transfer mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, BCRs, adequacy, etc).
- Console telemetry: scope (admin events vs customer-instrumented events), retention period, and sample schema for telemetry exported from the Redwood Console.
- Cookies / tracking on the hosted SDK: categories (essential/analytics/marketing), purpose descriptions, and whether cookie IDs are shared with downstream processors.
- Any SOC 2 / ISO / audit report access or attestations related to logging and telemetry.

Can you send a single email with the attachments and a one-page summary we can drop into our assessment? If you'd prefer, we can do a 30-minute call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lim
Threat & Privacy Manager | ACME Marketing
[Attachment requested: subprocessors spreadsheet + sample telemetry schema]

-----

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — cookies & marketing telemetry for DPA

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact package that should cover the assessment items: subprocessors CSV, a short data flow / DDI PDF for our telemetry, and a console retention sample export. Quick answers here while the attachments upload:

- Subprocessors: attached CSV includes all third-party services we use to process/route telemetry from the hosted SDK and Console (column headers: name, purpose, processing_location, contract_type).
- Transfers: Redwood stores production telemetry in regional clusters; for EU customers we keep data in our EU region by default. Where data is routed to US-based analytics backends (opt-in integrations) we rely on SCCs; our DPA lists SCCs as the mechanism.
- Console telemetry: primarily admin/operational events (login, api-key actions, route changes). Customer-instrumented telemetry (events you send from website SDKs) is forwarded to configured endpoints or processors by your integration and may include identifiers. Retention varies by telemetry type — see attached retention sample (console-retention-sample.json).
- Cookies / tracking: the SDK uses a small essential cookie for session continuity; analytics cookies are only set if you enable analytics integrations. We do not automatically sync cookie IDs to unrelated downstream processors without explicit integration configuration.
- Audit reports: we can provide SOC 2 Type II redacted report on NDA and point you at the security portal for the current cert.

If helpful, propose a 30-minute call Wednesday 15:00-15:30 PT (I can share screens of the Console telemetry UI and the SDK settings).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
[Attachments: subprocessors-export-2028-03.csv (csv), redwood-telemetry-ddi.pdf (pdf), console-retention-sample.json (json)]

Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request — cookies & marketing telemetry for DPA

Hi Tom / Sara — quick note from product/privacy side to be explicit:

- SDK behavior: Redwood's client SDK does not automatically collect PII fields (email/name) unless the customer's instrumentation explicitly includes those fields in the event payload. In other words, if ACME's frontend sends an event with an "email" property, that value will be present in the routed event and may be stored by processors you configure. The SDK itself will not mutate or enrich events with account-level PII.
- Console telemetry (admin events): collected for security and operational diagnostics only; retention for admin telemetry is 90 days by default for hosted accounts (can be extended on Dedicated/Private deployments).
- Data residency: for EU customers we offer EU-only storage and processing options; cross-border transfers only occur for integrations you opt into or where contractual configuration requires it. SCCs are the baseline transfer mechanism for any necessary EU->US flows.
- Logging access: raw debug logs that contain instrumented payloads are only accessible to support/engineers on a need basis and are tracked in audit logs; we can provide redacted samples for the assessment.

I'll attach a one-page summary to this thread and the DDI which Ben included should have the schema examples. Let me know if ACME would like a redaction example or a short packaged attestation we can sign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-telemetry-ddi.pdf (brief DDI + schema examples)]

I'll slot time for a walk-through Wednesday 15:00 PT unless you'd prefer a different time.

- We'd like a short attestation (one paragraph) confirming that Redwood will not surface raw customer PII via the Console UI and that admin telemetry retained for diagnostics is restricted to operational metadata unless explicitly included by the customer's instrumentation.
- Please confirm the default retention (90 days) can be set to 180 days for our tenant — we'll decide after the call.
- We'll sign the DPA; please send DocuSign link to legal@acme-marketing.com and include the SCC addendum we discussed.
